mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a single month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically lower than the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in any month for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two consecutive months indicate disinflation, prompting central banks to hold rates steady and allowing equity discount rates to normalize, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically higher than the 20-day forward returns during the prior disinflationary period (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not remain below 3% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) by more than 20,000 jobs in a single month coincides with stronger wage growth expectations, lowering risk premia and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >20,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 70% of such monthly events (binomial test p > 0.05), or wage growth (UNRATE) does not rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals weakening aggregate demand, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the following month are not significantly lower than the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05), or INDPRO recovers >3% in the next two months.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 3% suggests supply-side expansion that outpaces demand, reducing forward discounting pressure and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows at a rate >3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically higher than the 20-day forward returns during the prior three months of sub-3% growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both unemployment (UNRATE) and consumer confidence proxies (not available in this catalog) would typically reinforce demand, but here we proxy with a combined signal: when UNRATE falls by 0.2pp and HOUST rises by 5% in the same month, it predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by ≥0.2pp and HOUST increases by ≥5% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market tightening and rising business activity
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 80% of such monthly events (binomial test p > 0.05), or either proxy moves in the opposite direction in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling real yields (implied by a flattening yield curve, not directly observable here) is proxied by a downward trend in the 2-year Treasury yield proxy (not available). As an alternative, a sustained decline in the 10-year yield proxy (not available). Instead, we use FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 jointly: when FEDFUNDS stays below 4% while GDP momentum (GDPC1) accelerates for three months, it predicts positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns due to lower discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.0% for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05) during such regimes, or either proxy breaks the pattern in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in job openings (not directly observable) is often proxied by a surge in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a concurrent rise in unemployment benefits claims (not available). Here, we use PAYEMS and RSAFS jointly: when PAYEMS rises by >10,000 and RSAFS increases by >50,000 in the same month, it signals a tight labor market that supports equity risk appetite, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 and RSAFS increases by >50,000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 70% of such monthly events (binomial test p > 0.05), or either proxy moves in the opposite direction in the subsequent month.
